title: Preserve saved destinations
summary: Keep the existing return flow working while accepting a saved destination.
actionsIntro: Both changes keep the existing return path in control, so current destination checks still decide where a request may go.

actions.title: Keep existing checks
actions.description: Retain current destination validation for every caller.

actions.title: Support saved destinations
actions.description: Accept the saved destination through the existing return path.
actions.technical: After validation succeeds, the handler uses the existing return route. It does not add a separate redirect path.

success.title: Existing flows still work
success.description: Current callers keep their return behavior.
success.technical: Check both paths against current results before treating this outcome as verified.

success.title: Saved destination returns
success.description: The requested destination reaches the existing return path.

boundary: Code changes and focused checks only. Deployment needs separate approval.

risks.title: Caller behavior may differ
risks.description: The full plan names the callers that need separate verification.
risks.technical: A saved value could take a shortcut that current callers do not use. Check both paths before treating the shared behavior as verified.

risksIntro: The main confidence gap is whether saved and caller-provided values follow the same checks across all callers.

questions.title: Confirm missing-value behavior
questions.description: Should an absent saved destination keep the existing fallback?
questions.technical: The return description covers valid saved values, so confirm this branch instead of inferring it.

details.intro: The deeper sections explain where destination checks run, how a valid saved value returns to its caller, and which cases still need verification.
